newsitem.title: FINLAND: NOKIA TO SUPPLY DIGITAL DECODERS TO SPAIN.
newsitem.headline: NOKIA TO SUPPLY DIGITAL DECODERS TO SPAIN.

text.p: Finnish telecoms group Nokia Oy said in a statement on Wednesday it would deliver 50,000 digital TV decoders to Spanish broadcasting company Via Digital.
It did not give the value of the deal.

"Some 50,000 Mediamaster digital decoders will be delivered in time for the launch of the Spanish service in September," Nokia said, referring to Via Digital's plan to be able to offer more than 70 television channels to to subscribers in September.
Nokia said its decoding equipment had been chosen because it "supported the common interface for conditional access", meaning that the same digital decoder could be used for many services.
The news comes as a battle over TV decoders is heating up between Spanish and French firms over which kind of decoders should be used to unscramble encrypted TV channels.
Spain's Telefonica and state television RTVE have won backing from the Spanish government for the multicrypt system which Nokia supplies.
That has prompted a complaint to the European Commission by an operation backed by French pay-Television operator Canal Plus which wants its simulcrypt system to be used.
Via Digital is a new company formed by Telefonica, RTVE, Mexican media conglomerate Televisa and some other media publishers, Nokia said.
Nokia said its open standard provided end-users with the opportunity to subscribe to a range of services offered by a number of companies instead of being tide to a single supplier.

Its Mediamaster 9601 was "the first statellite receiver and multimedia terminal of its kind available today to be fully compatible with the digital video broadcasting standard ... and common interface," Nokia said.
Nokia said its branded digital decoders would be available for rental at more than 6,000 outlets throughout Spain.
